title: Configure TypeScript for server and client
description: TypeScript needs separate configs for server (Node, ESM, targeting dist/server/) and client (DOM, lit decorators, targeting dist/public/). A root tsconfig.json for IDE support, with tsconfig.server.json and tsconfig.client.json extending it for build-specific settings.
design: Root tsconfig sets strict:true, moduleResolution:bundler. Server extends root with target:ES2022, lib:[ES2022], types:[node]. Client extends root with target:ES2022, lib:[ES2022,DOM,DOM.Iterable], useDefineForClassFields:true for Lit decorators.
acceptance_criteria: tsc --project tsconfig.server.json compiles without errors on empty stubs. tsc --project tsconfig.client.json compiles without errors. IDE picks up types correctly for both src/server and src/client.
close_reason: TypeScript configured: tsconfig.json with strict/isolatedModules, separate server and client configs

title: Configure Biome for linting and formatting
description: Biome replaces ESLint and Prettier. Must be configured for the project conventions: 2-space indentation, single quotes, no semicolons. Applies to all TypeScript files in src/ and tests/. pnpm lint runs biome check. pnpm lint:fix runs biome check --write.
design: biome.json at repo root. Formatter: indentStyle=space, indentWidth=2, quoteStyle=single, semicolons=asNeeded. Linter enabled with recommended rules. Files: includes src/ and tests/.
acceptance_criteria: biome.json present. pnpm lint passes on a correctly-formatted TypeScript file. pnpm lint fails on a file with double quotes or semicolons. pnpm lint:fix auto-corrects formatting.
close_reason: Biome configured: 2-space, single quotes, no semis, covers src/tests/root config files

title: Configure Vite for dev proxy and production build
description: Vite needs two modes: dev (port 5173, proxies /api and /events to Hono at 3003) and prod (outputs to dist/public/). index.html lives at repo root referencing src/client/main.ts. The server tsup build outputs to dist/server/.
design: vite.config.ts uses server.proxy for /api and /events in dev. build.outDir set to dist/public. tsup config in package.json scripts: tsup src/server/index.ts --format esm --outDir dist/server.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm dev proxies /api requests to :3003 in browser. pnpm build creates dist/public/index.html and dist/server/index.js. Source maps enabled for both.
close_reason: Vite configured: dev proxy for /api+/events, dist/public output, SSE timeouts, cross-platform chmod, resolve conditions

title: Initialize pnpm project and install all dependencies
description: Bootstrap the npm package. Run pnpm init, set name to beads-dashboard, configure engines (node>=20), then install all deps: vite, lit, @material/web, hono, @hono/node-server, tsup, tsx, concurrently, chokidar, execa for runtime; @types/node, typescript, @vitest/coverage-v8, vitest, @playwright/test, biome for dev. Set up the directory structure from the design spec.
design: Single pnpm package (not workspace). tsup for server, Vite for client. execa for spawning bd CLI processes.
acceptance_criteria: package.json exists with correct name/engines. pnpm install completes without errors. All dirs (src/server, src/client/board, src/client/epic, src/client/task, src/client/ui, src/client/store, tests/unit, tests/e2e) created.
close_reason: pnpm project initialized, all deps installed, directory structure created

title: Set up project scaffolding and dual build pipeline
description: The project requires a reproducible development environment before any implementation can start. Covers pnpm init, all dependency installation (Vite, Lit, Material Web, Hono, tsup, Biome, chokidar, execa, concurrently, tsx), Vite config for dev and prod, TypeScript config, and Biome config (2-space indent, single quotes, no semis).
acceptance_criteria: pnpm dev starts both Vite (5173) and Hono (3003) with /api proxy. pnpm build produces dist/public/ and dist/server/. pnpm lint runs Biome and passes on empty project. TypeScript compiles without errors.
close_reason: All setup tasks complete: pnpm init, TypeScript, Vite, Biome configs done

title: Write E2E tests for board rendering and SSE updates
description: Playwright tests that assert the dashboard works end-to-end against the seeded temp bd project. Test: board renders with correct epic swim lanes and columns, tasks appear in correct columns based on status, subtask tally shows correct counts, a bd status change (via bd update in the test) propagates via SSE and updates the UI without page reload.
design: Tests in tests/e2e/*.spec.ts. Use page.waitForSelector for initial render. For SSE test: change a task status via execa bd update, then wait for UI to reflect change (page.waitForFunction or locator assertion with timeout). Seed data from global setup is the known ground truth for assertions.
acceptance_criteria: Test: epic swim lanes render with correct titles and status summaries. Test: tasks in correct columns (open=blocked, ready, in-progress, done). Test: subtask tally shows '1 of 3 complete' for seeded task. Test: bd update status change reflects in UI within 2 seconds via SSE. All E2E tests pass.
close_reason: 7 E2E tests pass: epic lanes, columns, subtask tally, SSE update. Fixed bd where multiline parsing and switched to streamSSE

title: Configure Playwright and implement E2E global setup
description: Playwright E2E tests need a global setup that bootstraps a fully standalone beads project: creates a temp dir, runs bd init, seeds known epics/tasks/subtasks via bd create commands, starts the beads-dashboard server pointed at the temp dir, and stores the server URL in a global fixture. Teardown kills the server and deletes the temp dir.
design: playwright.config.ts at repo root. globalSetup: tests/e2e/setup/global-setup.ts. Uses child_process or execa to run bd init and bd create seed commands. Server started as a child process, URL stored in process.env.BEADS_TEST_URL. Seed data is deterministic: 2 epics, 5 tasks (mix of statuses), 3 subtasks on one task.
acceptance_criteria: E2E setup completes in <30s. Seed data is consistent across runs. Teardown cleans up temp dir and kills server process. Tests can access server URL via fixture. Works on macOS and Linux CI.
close_reason: Playwright configured: global setup seeds 2 epics/5 tasks/3 subtasks, server on 3099, teardown cleans up, placeholder test passes in 12s

title: Configure Vitest with v8 coverage at 85% threshold
description: Vitest is the unit/component test runner. Must be configured with @vitest/coverage-v8 provider and 85% threshold across all four metrics (lines, functions, branches, statements). pnpm test runs vitest and fails if coverage drops below threshold. Separate config from playwright.
design: vitest.config.ts at repo root. coverage.provider='v8', coverage.thresholds={lines:85,functions:85,branches:85,statements:85}. coverage.include=['src/**']. Test files in tests/unit/ and tests/component/ (component tests TBD — Lit testing utilities needed).
acceptance_criteria: pnpm test runs and reports coverage. Build fails if any metric is below 85%. Coverage report generated in coverage/ directory. vitest.config.ts is separate from vite.config.ts (or extends it minimally).
close_reason: Vitest configured with v8 coverage, 85% threshold, scoped to src/server

title: Implement task card and subtask tally components (src/client/task/)
description: Implement bd-task-card and bd-subtask-tally. TDD approach: write component tests first (tests/component/task-card.test.ts) verifying data from context by bead-id, priority chip colours, tally hidden when no subtasks, then implement. Uses md-card from Material Web. Priority chips use Catppuccin colours.
design: bd-task-card uses md-card from Material Web. Priority shown as a coloured chip using Catppuccin colours (P0=red, P1=orange, P2=yellow, P3=green, P4=surface). bd-subtask-tally is a small inline indicator, hidden if task has no subtasks. Assignee shown as initials avatar if present.
acceptance_criteria: bd-task-card renders title, ID, assignee, priority chip, and subtask tally. bd-subtask-tally shows correct counts from context (e.g. 2 of 10 complete). Tally hidden when subtask count is 0. Priority chip colour matches priority level. Updates when context changes.
close_reason: task-card+subtask-tally: priority chips, subtaskDone correct, 20 tests pass

title: Implement epic swim lane component (src/client/epic/epic-lane.ts)
description: Implement bd-epic-lane — full-width swim lane spanning all 4 columns. TDD approach: write component test first (tests/component/epic-lane.test.ts) verifying title and status summary render from mock context, then implement. Status summary computed from task counts per status (no server round-trip).
design: Full-width CSS grid row spanning all columns. Status summary computed from task counts per status in context — no server round-trip. Material Web typography tokens for the epic title. Visually distinct from task cards (different background, larger text).
acceptance_criteria: bd-epic-lane spans all 4 columns. Epic title renders from context. Status summary correctly counts tasks by status (e.g. '2 in progress, 5 done'). Updates when board context changes. Looks visually distinct from task cards.
close_reason: epic-lane: spans 4 cols, status summary from context, 6 tests pass

title: Implement board layout and column components (src/client/board/)
description: Implement bd-board (layout shell) and bd-column (kanban column). TDD approach: write component tests first (tests/component/board.test.ts, column.test.ts) verifying renders with mock context, then implement. Both consume board context. CSS grid layout. Material Web for chrome. Catppuccin Mocha colours.
design: bd-board uses CSS grid: 4 columns for the kanban layout, with epic lane rows spanning all 4. bd-column is a display component receiving column name as attribute. Both consume board context to get their data by ID. Material Web card/surface for column chrome. Catppuccin Mocha CSS custom properties for colours.
acceptance_criteria: bd-board renders one bd-epic-lane per epic in board state. bd-column renders correct tasks for its column/epic combination. Layout is CSS grid with 4 equal-width columns. Components update when context changes.
close_reason: bd-board+column: 4-col grid in epic-lane, filterTasksByEpic exported, experimentalDecorators fix, 11 tests pass

title: Implement Lit context and board store (src/client/store/)
description: Implement Lit context (context.ts) and board store (board-store.ts). TDD approach: write tests first (tests/unit/board-store.test.ts) verifying SSE event handling and state updates, then implement. BoardStore extends LitElement as ContextProvider. State is reactive. EventSource opened in connectedCallback, closed on disconnect.
design: Use @lit/context. BoardStore extends LitElement and acts as ContextProvider. State is a reactive property — any change triggers re-render in consuming components. EventSource opened in connectedCallback, closed in disconnectedCallback. On board-update: parse JSON and set this.boardState = newState.
acceptance_criteria: BoardStore provides context to all descendant components. board-update SSE event updates context and consuming components re-render. EventSource reconnects automatically on disconnect (browser native behavior). TypeScript types cover all fields used by components.
close_reason: board-store + context implemented: Lit ContextProvider, SSE EventSource lifecycle, error handling, tests pass

title: Implement bin entrypoint (src/server/index.ts)
description: index.ts is the CLI entrypoint. It parses --open and --port flags from process.argv, auto-discovers the .beads/ directory via `bd where` falling back to CWD, starts the Hono server on the resolved port (default 3003), logs the server URL, and optionally opens the browser. Must have #!/usr/bin/env node shebang as the first line.
design: Parse argv manually (no arg parser library needed for two flags). bd where run via execa to get beads path — if it fails, fall back to process.cwd(). Use open package or child_process.exec('open URL') for --open on macOS/Linux. Shebang line must be first — tsup preserves it with --banner.js option.
acceptance_criteria: node dist/server/index.js starts server and logs URL. --open flag opens default browser. --port 4000 starts on 4000. If .beads/ not found, starts anyway with a warning (dashboard shows empty state). Ctrl+C exits cleanly.
close_reason: index.ts: parseArgs, bd where discovery, serve+watcher+SSE wired, shebang via tsup.config.ts, 6 tests pass

title: Implement Hono app with routes (src/server/app.ts)
description: app.ts creates and exports the Hono application with three routes: GET /api/board returns current board state as JSON (calls getBoardState()), GET /events handles SSE connection (delegates to sse.ts), GET /* serves static files from dist/public/ in production. In dev, the Vite dev server handles static files via proxy.
design: Use @hono/node-server for static file serving (serveStatic). Route order: /api/board first, /events second, wildcard last. app.ts exports the Hono instance. Server startup is in index.ts, not app.ts, so app is testable without starting a port.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/board returns 200 with JSON body matching BoardState type. GET /events returns text/event-stream content-type. GET /nonexistent returns 404. GET / serves index.html in production. CORS not needed (same origin).
close_reason: app.ts: /api/board, /events (SSE ReadableStream), static serving, 7 tests pass

title: Implement SSE endpoint and client registry (src/server/sse.ts)
description: sse.ts manages SSE client registry and broadcasting. TDD approach: write tests first (tests/unit/sse.test.ts) using mock response writers, then implement. Tests verify: client registration, broadcast reaches all clients, dead clients removed on disconnect. Event name: board-update, full payload each time.
design: Use Hono's streaming response for SSE. Registry is a Set of response writers. On each board change: call getBoardState(), serialize to JSON, send as 'data: {...}\n\n'. Event name: board-update. No delta diffing — always send full payload. Client disconnect detected via request abort signal.
acceptance_criteria: New browser connection appears in registry. board-update event sent to all connected clients when watcher fires. Disconnected client (tab closed) is removed from registry within one event cycle. Multiple simultaneous clients all receive the same update.
close_reason: sse.ts implemented TDD: addClient/broadcast/clientCount with AbortSignal cleanup, 8 tests pass

title: Implement .beads/ file watcher with debounce (src/server/watcher.ts)
description: watcher.ts uses chokidar to watch .beads/ directory, debounced at 300ms. TDD approach: write tests first (tests/unit/watcher.test.ts) using vi.useFakeTimers to test debounce behaviour, then implement. Returns a cleanup function. Tests verify: rapid changes = one callback, quiet period = callback fires.
design: chokidar.watch('.beads/', {ignoreInitial:true}). Debounce using setTimeout/clearTimeout pattern — no lodash dependency. Watcher is created with a beadsDir path and onChange callback. Returns a cleanup function to stop watching.
acceptance_criteria: onChange fires once for a burst of rapid file changes within 300ms. onChange fires after 300ms quiet period following a change. Watcher cleanup function stops chokidar and prevents further callbacks. Works on macOS (FSEvents) and Linux (inotify).
close_reason: watcher.ts implemented TDD: chokidar + 300ms debounce, cleanup cancels pending callbacks, 6 tests pass

title: Implement bd CLI query wrappers (src/server/query.ts)
description: query.ts provides typed wrappers around bd CLI commands using execa. TDD approach: write tests first (tests/unit/query.test.ts), then implement. Key queries: list all epics, list tasks by status, get subtask counts per task. Uses bd sql --json or bd list --json. Mock execa in tests with vi.mock.
design: Use execa to spawn bd with --json flag. Parse stdout as JSON. Define TypeScript interfaces for Epic, Task, BoardState in this file or a types.ts sibling. Handle bd not found in PATH with a clear error message. bd manages Dolt server lifecycle transparently — no server start needed.
acceptance_criteria: getBoardState() returns typed BoardState with epics array and tasks grouped by status. Function throws descriptive error if bd not in PATH. Execa spawn errors are wrapped with context. All return types are explicit TypeScript interfaces (no any).
close_reason: query.ts implemented TDD: getBoardState() with ready/blocked split, subtask counts, error handling, 13 tests pass

title: Implement unit, component, and E2E test suites
description: Full test coverage before publication. Vitest with v8 coverage at 85% threshold (lines, functions, branches, statements). Unit tests cover query.ts, watcher.ts, sse.ts with execa mocked. Component tests verify Lit rendering with context values and attribute changes. Playwright E2E bootstraps a real temp bd project (bd init, seed via bd create, start server), asserts known data renders correctly, verifies SSE updates propagate to UI.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm test passes with >=85% coverage across all metrics. pnpm test:e2e passes against a freshly bootstrapped temp bd project. E2E teardown removes temp dir and kills server cleanly.
close_reason: All test tasks complete: Vitest unit tests, Playwright E2E setup and tests

title: Build Lit frontend with kanban board components
description: Lit web component frontend with a kanban board. State lives in board-store.ts (outside component tree), distributed via Lit Context API. Components are display-only and receive bead IDs as attributes/properties to look up their own data slice from context. Material Web Components for UI primitives. Four columns: Open (blocked tasks), Ready, In Progress, Done. Epics render as full-width swim lanes. Subtask progress shown as a tally (e.g. 2 of 10 complete) on task cards.
acceptance_criteria: Board renders columns and epic swim lanes. Task cards show title, ID, assignee, priority, subtask tally. SSE updates from the store reflect in the UI without page reload. Components are display-only — no state mutation in components.
close_reason: All frontend tasks complete: board-store, board/column, epic-lane, task-card, subtask-tally

title: Implement Hono server with SSE realtime updates
description: The server is the core runtime: serves the dashboard, queries beads data via bd CLI (execa), watches .beads/ for file changes (chokidar, debounced 300ms), and pushes board-update SSE events to all connected clients. Routes: GET /api/board (initial state), GET /events (SSE stream), GET /* (static files from dist/public/). Default port 3003.
acceptance_criteria: Server starts and serves index.html. /api/board returns typed board JSON. /events streams board-update on .beads/ file change. Changes debounced — rapid file writes trigger only one bd call. --open flag opens browser. --port overrides default 3003.
close_reason: All server tasks complete: query.ts, watcher.ts, sse.ts, app.ts, index.ts

title: Validate npx end-to-end flow
description: Smoke test the full npx experience in a real project context. Run npm pack to produce the tarball, then npx ./beads-dashboard-*.tgz in a temp directory with a real bd project initialized. Verify the server starts, the browser can load the board, and SSE updates work. Also test --open and --port flags.
design: Manual validation task — no automated test needed here (E2E tests cover behaviour; this validates the packaging/distribution layer). Use a real bd project with actual issues (can use this repo's own .beads/).
acceptance_criteria: npx ./beads-dashboard-*.tgz starts server on 3003. Dashboard loads in browser and shows real beads data. SSE updates work. --open opens browser. --port changes port. No errors in server console. Works without global npm install.

title: Configure package.json for npm distribution
description: Finalise package.json for publication: name=beads-dashboard, bin={beads-dashboard: dist/server/index.js}, files=[dist/], engines={node:>=20}, type=module. Add README documenting bd as a prerequisite and the npx usage. Ensure dist/server/index.js has #!/usr/bin/env node shebang (via tsup --banner) and is executable (chmod +x in postbuild script).
design: tsup config: banner.js='#!/usr/bin/env node'. postbuild script: chmod +x dist/server/index.js. README documents: prerequisites (bd installed), usage (npx beads-dashboard [--open] [--port N]), what it shows (kanban board of bd tasks).
acceptance_criteria: npm pack produces a tarball containing only dist/ and package.json. node dist/server/index.js executes without permission error. npx beads-dashboard --help shows usage. README covers prerequisites and usage.

title: Configure and validate npm package for npx distribution
description: The end goal is npx beads-dashboard working from any project with bd installed. Requires correct package.json (name: beads-dashboard, bin entry, files: [dist/], engines: node>=20), shebang on dist/server/index.js, executable permissions, and validation of the full npx flow. bd is a peer dependency documented but not enforced.
acceptance_criteria: npx beads-dashboard starts server in a project with .beads/. npx beads-dashboard --open also opens the browser. npx beads-dashboard --port 4000 uses port 4000. Published package contains only dist/ and package.json.
